title: Relative Grounds for Refusal of Trade Mark Registration
content:
Section 11 of the Trade Marks Act, 1999 prohibits the registration of a trade mark if: (a) its identity or similarity to an earlier trade mark and the identity or similarity of goods/services causes a likelihood of confusion or association among the public; or (b) it is identical or similar to an earlier well-known trade mark in India.

Key Legal Implications for Ayurveda & Pharmaceuticals:
1. In Cadila Health Care Ltd. v. Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (2001), the Supreme Court emphasized that a stricter standard of confusing similarity must be applied to medicinal and pharmaceutical products to prevent consumer confusion that could endanger health.
2. For Ayurvedic medicines, phonetic, visual, and conceptual similarities with registered Ayurvedic or allopathic brand names in Class 5 (pharmaceuticals/herbal medicines) or Class 3 (herbal cosmetics) are rigorously examined by the Trade Marks Registry.
3. Prior trade mark search across the official IP India Trade Marks Journal is essential before launching commercial Ayurvedic branding.
